newsitem.title: BURUNDI: U.N. envoy has talks with Burundian leaders.
newsitem.headline: U.N. envoy has talks with Burundian leaders.

text.p: U.N. special envoy Mohamed Sahnoun held talks on Monday with Burundian government leaders, military officials and opposition politicians on peace efforts in the war-ravaged Central African country.
Sahnoun, who met President Pierre Buyoya on Sunday night, told Reuters he had come to assess the progress of the peace plan.
Sahnoun, joint special representative of the United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity (OAU) to the Great Lakes region, said:
"I met with President Buyoya last night and our meeting was very thorough. We were able to discuss all issues related to Burundi and the peace process."
He said he would have more talks on Monday with leaders before leaving for Tanzania for consultations on Burundi with mediator and former Tanzanian president Julius Nyerere.
Burundi's Tutsi-dominated army and Hutu rebels are fighting for a greater political stake in the ethnically divided tea and coffee-growing country.
About 150,000 people, mainly civilians caught in the middle, have died since 1993 when Tutsi soldiers murdered the first freely elected president, Melchior Ndadaye, a Hutu.

Asked what Buyoya's attitude was towards serious negotiations with Hutu rebels, who mainly constitute Leonard Nyangoma's National Council for the Defence of Democracy (CNDD), Sahnoun said: "I think he is willing to participate in the talks. He is serious as far as I am concerned."
Marking the first anniversary last Friday of a bloodless coup that brought him to power, Buyoya promised to work for peace and unity.
